silo_relevance: This paper is relevant to simulation_monte_carlo because it studies quantum amplitude estimation as a way to estimate an expectation value, directly contrasting its sample-efficiency with Monte Carlo-style estimation. It also highlights the practical simulation bottlenecks that matter for Monte Carlo workflows: finite sampling resolution, qubit growth, and hardware-dependent circuit overhead.

key_points.point: QAE is used to estimate a bond expectation value, making it a direct quantum alternative to Monte Carlo-style expectation estimation.
key_points.silo_note: For simulation_monte_carlo, the key relevance is that the paper frames expectation estimation as a sampling problem and uses amplitude estimation to target the same quantity Monte Carlo would estimate.

key_points.point: The paper explicitly contrasts QAE with Monte Carlo by noting the sample burden of quantum Monte Carlo and the convergence advantage of amplitude estimation.
key_points.silo_note: This matters because the silo is about simulation methods: the paper positions QAE as a more sample-efficient estimator while also acknowledging that Monte Carlo-style methods still face heavy sampling and qubit-scaling costs.

key_points.point: Finite evaluation-qubit resolution limits the quality of the simulated estimate, preventing exact recovery of the target probability in the toy example.
key_points.silo_note: For simulation_monte_carlo, this is important because it shows that even quantum simulation of an expectation value can be discretization-limited, affecting how accurately a Monte Carlo replacement can resolve probabilities.

key_points.point: The simulation cost is strongly hardware-dependent, with two-qubit gate overhead varying by architecture and topology.
key_points.silo_note: This matters to simulation_monte_carlo because practical simulation performance is not just about algorithmic sample complexity; circuit depth and entangling-gate count can dominate feasibility on real devices.

key_points.point: Routing and SWAP overhead are a major limitation for scalable simulation on superconducting hardware, while heuristic routing is only a partial remedy.
key_points.silo_note: For simulation_monte_carlo, this highlights that implementing Monte Carlo-like quantum simulation at scale is constrained by compilation/routing overhead, which can erase theoretical gains.
